newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank steady to firmer on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank steady to firmer on foreign demand.

text.p: The interbank rate were steady to higher late on Tuesday as some foreign custodians sought baht to settle stock transactions of foreign buyers, dealers said.
But they expected the overnight rate to soften after the central bank issued stop-gap measures requiring all dealings in the bourse's foreign board to be settle in US dollars only.

The move was aimed at plugging a loophole through which baht could be siphoned out of the system by speculators who had were now in need of funds to cover their short positions. The central bank has cut off baht supply to foreign speculators.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted around 12.00-13.50 percent late against 12.00-13.00 percent early.
"Foreign banks bid actively. Many believe this could be linked to the settlement of heavy foreign selling recently to acquire the baht," said a dealer from one major local bank.
Foreign players who dumped baht heavily in May on anticiption that the baht would be devalued were said to be seeking baht to cover their one-month forward positions due later this week.
The baht offshore firmed to 24.050/24.250 late from 24.240/24.340 after the news of central bank's new measures.
But the baht in the domestic market eased to 25.743/25.753 to the dollar from 25.725/25.735 as the greenback rebounded.
Dealers expected the baht in the offshore market to strengthen further as the quest for baht continued and all access virtually closed.
"Well, there is one channel left for speculators who shorted on baht. They can come to Thailand disguised as tourists and smuggle the baht out," one dealer joked.
The one-month swap premium in the offshore markets was quoted around 95/115 satangs per dollar from 115/130 satangs this morning. -- Anchalee Koetsawang (662) 652-0642
